evidence.observation: The whole module is this one function. It normalizes the requested path (backslashes to forward slashes), detects a path that is already inside the workspace real root via the exact boundary `normalizedRequested === workspace || startsWith(workspace + '/')`, and otherwise re-roots the request under the workspace. It returns { candidatePath, pathMode } for three modes: 'workspace-absolute', 'workspace-root-relative' (leading slash) and 'workspace-relative'. It deliberately performs no containment rejection of its own: `../..`, encoded separators and null bytes pass through unchanged, so safety must be established by the caller. That makes it the resolution half of the traversal contract that this fixture pins.

The repository's other path-safety helper. It resolves the base and the sanitized user path, then computes `relative(base, target)` and rejects with null when the relative path starts with '..' (or contains a `..` segment). This is the canonical containment predicate that the generated-file contract mirrors: resolve first, then prove the result is a descendant of the root rather than a sibling or ancestor.

Second half of the download gate: once a candidate is proven to be inside the workspace it is lower-cased, split into segments, and rejected if any segment is a denied name/directory or the final name is `.env`/`.env.*`. Together with the containment test this is what makes the generated-file route's allow-list decision; the fixture exercises the containment half of that decision.

The live enforcement point for generated-file downloads. After `resolveGeneratedFileCandidatePath` produces `candidatePath`, the handler runs `realpath` on it and computes `posix.relative(workspaceReal, targetReal)`, then rejects with 403 when the relative path is empty, '..', starts with '../', or is absolute. This is exactly the containment contract encoded by `normalizeGeneratedFilePath` in the new fixture, and it is why a bare `resolveGeneratedFileCandidatePath` result is not by itself a safe path.

The new normalized operation added by this task. It rejects empty paths, embedded null bytes and encoded separator/traversal tokens (`%2e`, `%2f`, `%5c`, `%00`) before calling `resolveGeneratedFileCandidatePath`, then applies the handler's `posix.relative` containment predicate and returns either { ok: false, reason } or an accepted { ok: true, candidatePath, pathMode, relativePath } that is guaranteed to be a strict descendant of the workspace root.

The traversal / encoded-separator case table. Unsafe rows cover plain `../` traversal, backslash and leading-slash traversal, the workspace root itself, encoded `%2e%2e%2f` / `%5c` / `%2f` sequences (upper and lower case), an encoded null byte, a raw null byte and the empty path; valid rows cover workspace-relative, root-relative and absolute generated paths plus spaces, an interior `.`-segment and a sibling-prefix path (`<root>-evil/x.pdf`) that must be re-rooted instead of escaping.

The executable fixture. It runs on Node's built-in `node:test` runner (no dev dependency needed), asserts each reject row fails with the expected reason and each accept row resolves to the expected relativePath/pathMode, and adds two invariant tests: every accepted candidate is a strict descendant of the root with no `..` segment, and the normalized operation results are printed as a table.

claims.claim: `resolveGeneratedFileCandidatePath` only normalizes and re-roots a requested path into a candidate; it never rejects unsafe input, so the generated-file traversal guarantee depends on a containment check performed by the caller (the `posix.relative` guard in server/handlers/files.js).

`safePath` establishes the repository's canonical containment predicate: resolve the target, compute `relative(base, target)`, and reject (return null) when the relative path escapes with `..`, which is the same resolve-then-prove-inside shape the new generated-file contract reproduces.

The new `normalizeGeneratedFilePath` contract rejects traversal, encoded-separator (`%2e`/`%2f`/`%5c`/`%00`) and null-byte requests before resolution, and accepts valid workspace-relative, root-relative and absolute generated paths while guaranteeing every accepted candidate stays inside the intended workspace root.

The executable fixture encodes the contract as a case table plus invariant checks and passes end-to-end: all 20 assertions in server/utils/generated-file-path.traversal.test.js succeed, so unsafe paths are rejected and valid generated paths remain inside the intended root.

conclusion: The traversal / encoded-separator contract for generated-file paths is now pinned as an executable fixture. `resolveGeneratedFileCandidatePath` performs normalization only (workspace-absolute / workspace-root-relative / workspace-relative), so the fixture composes it with the handler's `posix.relative` containment predicate and adds pre-resolution rejection of encoded separators, encoded/raw null bytes and empty paths. Twelve unsafe cases are rejected with a stable reason and eight valid generated paths are accepted with `candidatePath` proven to be a strict descendant of the fixture workspace root, including a sibling-prefix path that is re-rooted rather than allowed to escape. All 20 assertions pass under `node --test`.

validation.notes: 20/20 assertions pass (12 reject cases, 6 accept cases, 2 invariant/demo tests) in ~72ms on Node v24.14.0. The fixture uses only Node built-ins (`node:test`, `node:assert/strict`, `node:path`) plus the repository module under test, so it needs no installed dependencies. Limitation: `node_modules/` is absent in this workspace, so vitest is not available (`import('vitest')` fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND); the pre-existing vitest suite `server/utils/generated-file-path.test.js` was therefore not executed and was left unmodified. No dependencies were installed and no package/lock or git configuration files were touched.
